The Medtronic parser quarantined 1,540 malformed records. DiaData excluded all 18 DDATSHR-source participants before eligibility assessment. Excluded participants and per-source availability are retained in the supplementary tables.

forecast_results_text: The lowest point-estimate MAEs were ddatshr at 30 minutes: Stack (17.11 mg/dL); ddatshr at 60 minutes: Stack (29.61 mg/dL); ddatshr at 90 minutes: TFTEncoder (38.11 mg/dL); diadata at 30 minutes: Ridge (22.07 mg/dL); diadata at 60 minutes: Ridge (33.48 mg/dL); diadata at 90 minutes: TFTEncoder (40.69 mg/dL). These rankings are descriptive, not multiplicity-adjusted pairwise superiority claims.
hypothesis_results_text: RF HR − RF CGM showed a Holm-significant improvement in 0/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6; Stack − RF showed a Holm-significant improvement in 3/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6; RF − persistence showed a Holm-significant improvement in 4/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6. Failure to reject is not evidence of equivalence.
primary_summary: After correction across 18 tests, adding HR improved RF in 0/6 cohort–horizon comparisons, while stacking improved RF in 3/6. The stack findings were ddatshr: 3/3 horizons; diadata: 0/3 horizons.
seed_results_text: Across individual RF training seeds, 30-minute subject-macro MAE ranged 18.12–18.15 mg/dL for ddatshr; 23.92–23.95 mg/dL for diadata. Full seed-specific results are supplied, rather than treating seeds as additional patients.
heterogeneity_text: DDATSHR RF 30-minute participant RMSE ranged from 18.97 to 28.90 mg/dL. Participant 907 had RMSE 22.75 mg/dL (rank 13 of 17, highest error first), 1,305 eligible origins and 21.4 recorded days. Its source-grid glucose and HR missing fractions were 16.3% and 7.2%, and eligible-input glucose SD was 73.27 mg/dL. Actual sensor labels were Abbott and Medtronic. These measurements replace the earlier inference from a small, device-selected sample; they do not identify a physiological cause. Exploratory Spearman associations with participant RMSE were ddatshr: recent absolute glucose rate rho=0.92, glucose SD rho=0.28, glucose missing fraction rho=0.13, HR missing fraction rho=0.02; diadata: recent absolute glucose rate rho=0.86, glucose SD rho=0.80, glucose missing fraction rho=-0.10, HR missing fraction rho=0.05. These cross-participant associations are unadjusted, may reflect source composition and do not establish causes of an individual participant’s error.
clarke_text: Zone A alone is not a complete error characterization: potentially important C, D and E errors remain visible in the full table and are not absorbed into a single A+B percentage.

sensitivity_text: The four-hour requirement retained 17 DDATSHR and 26 DiaData participants. The two history versions use the same longer-history eligible origins and participant allocations. Source transfer tests both directions between the seven primary D1NAMO and 22 HUPA-UCM participants; its training-source sizes are consequently unequal.
interval_text: Descriptive RF validation-residual interval coverage was ddatshr: 94.2%/94.2%/94.2% at 30/60/90 minutes (mean widths 103.3/171.1/210.9 mg/dL); diadata: 90.9%/90.8%/90.5% at 30/60/90 minutes (mean widths 136.3/195.0/238.1 mg/dL). These observed coverages are not assumed to equal their nominal 95% level.
generation_text: The fixed selection contained 135 cases from 46 people; 111 cases from 38 people formed the final test set. Development used 24 cases from 8 other people. Zero-shot and few-shot complete-contract acceptance was 100/111 and 96/111, respectively. The deterministic arm supplies a direct comparator with no language-model inference. All raw responses and request failures are retained, including rejected outputs.
generation_uncertainty_text: Giving each test participant equal weight, contract acceptance was zero_shot: 89.9% (95% interval 83.8–95.2%); few_shot: 86.0% (95% interval 78.9–92.1%). Intervals use 10,000 participant bootstrap resamples and are descriptive; three state-selected cases per person are not independent patients.
generation_errors_text: Rejected final completions included SHAP mismatches in 2 completions; direction mismatches in 25 completions; other_contract mismatches in 2 completions; tier mismatches in 1 completions. Categories can overlap within a completion. The prompt and detector were not modified in response to these final-test failures.
challenge_text: The separately designated challenge families produced 300 invalid contracts; 300 were rejected. Among 60 valid controls, 0 were rejected. All 30 source-corruption boundary cases were accepted despite deliberately wrong underlying HR values. Thus zero observed within-contract false negatives would not imply zero end-to-end factual errors. The development-family results are reported separately in the supplement.
discussion_results: After correction across 18 tests, adding HR improved RF in 0/6 cohort–horizon comparisons, while stacking improved RF in 3/6. The stack findings were ddatshr: 3/3 horizons; diadata: 0/3 horizons. RF HR − RF CGM showed a Holm-significant improvement in 0/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6; Stack − RF showed a Holm-significant improvement in 3/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6; RF − persistence showed a Holm-significant improvement in 4/6 cohort–horizon comparisons and a Holm-significant deterioration in 0/6. Failure to reject is not evidence of equivalence.
conclusion_text: After correction across 18 tests, adding HR improved RF in 0/6 cohort–horizon comparisons, while stacking improved RF in 3/6. The stack findings were ddatshr: 3/3 horizons; diadata: 0/3 horizons. Typed generation accepted 100/111 zero-shot and 96/111 few-shot test completions, while explicit source-corruption tests remained undetectable to a source-relative checker.
additional_results_text: AZT1D’s lowest point-estimate MAEs were 30 minutes: Stack, 15.06 mg/dL; 60 minutes: BiLSTMTransformer, 24.33 mg/dL; 90 minutes: BiLSTMTransformer, 30.34 mg/dL. Chronos-2 MAE on ddatshr was 19.70/34.33/45.04 mg/dL. Three-validator RF HR-minus-CGM differences on ddatshr were +0.17/+0.09/+0.05 mg/dL. Chronos-2 MAE on diadata was 23.85/36.23/45.37 mg/dL. Three-validator RF HR-minus-CGM differences on diadata were +0.21/+0.15/+0.10 mg/dL. These point estimates do not establish universal architecture superiority or HR equivalence. The supplementary tables retain all seeds, participant errors, glycemic ranges, Clarke zones and paired descriptive intervals.
latency_results_text: The 30 cases represented 24 participants. Median total processing times were deterministic: 0.124 s; few_shot: 26.659 s; zero_shot: 26.600 s. There were 0 observed deadline misses and 0 request errors across 90 measured runs. This small warm replay cannot establish hard real-time guarantees or patient benefit.
